name: text
description:
How text reads. Nine classes in the old vocabulary — title, section-title, lede, meta, mono-meta, digits and three eyebrows — declared only type properties: size, weight, colour, tracking, case. That is not nine components, it is one question with nine answers. The axis is named `variant` so the emitted class reads `text--lede`, one word from the name it replaces, rather than `text--role-lede`.

The eyebrow and the mono caption are the two type ideas the rest of the system kept re-deriving. Six composites had grown their own eyebrow at three sizes and two trackings, and nine had their own mono caption — none of that variance was chosen, it was each written at a call site and then extracted verbatim. A composite's eyebrow part now carries `text text--eyebrow` and declares only what is genuinely its own, which is usually just a colour.

section-title.$description: A band's heading. Weight 500, one step below `title` — at 600 it matched the page title and the eyebrow above it, so three levels of heading were one weight and the hierarchy was carried by size alone.

mono-meta.$description: A code-ish caption — a timestamp, an id, a file type. Nine units had their own; this is the one.

eyebrow.$description: The section eyebrow — the small uppercase line above a heading, in PARADISE, the second brand colour. ONE definition, because six composites had grown their own at three different sizes and two different trackings, none of which anyone chose: they were each written at a call site and then extracted verbatim. It was grey, with the brand colour parked in a second variant called `eyebrow` that 35 call sites reached for — which made the exception the common case. `eyebrow` is gone; this is it. `--color-eyebrow-ink` rather than `--color-secondary` because paradise at full strength fails on a sunflower-tinted panel, and an eyebrow lands on one.

eyebrow-quiet.$description: The eyebrow, one step down — for a surface that already has one.

label.$description: The label above a value — a stat's caption, a plan's name. Tighter tracking than the section eyebrow because it sits directly on the thing it names rather than above a block, and at that distance widest tracking reads as loose.

a11y.notes: `as` sets the element the caller needs for document structure — a heading level is a semantic decision the composition makes, not something a type role can decide for it. The role only says how it reads.
